attempts.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve production 2D game sprite animation. Image1 is the official sprite-pipeline reference canvas; Image2 is the approved seed character. Draw the WHOLE animation in one edit, exactly EIGHT distinct complete poses in ONE HORIZONTAL ROW in a wide transparent RGBA strip. Equal frame slots and transparent gutters, every tip/foot stays within its own slot. Same exact character identity, HD painterly mobile game style, face, eye colors, palette and materials, same 3/4 facing LEFT camera; no pixel-art, no labels, scenery, shadows, ground, poster. Keep one body scale and common world-space root across the strip; do not fit each pose separately or bottom-align moving parts. Actual anatomy and silhouette must change strongly and coherently through action, not the same original image wobbling. This is the seed's small olive-yellow bulb plant with TWO little glossy black eyes, four broad sage-green leaves atop its round bulb, one long large green LOOPED tendril and a second shorter curling tendril on its right, and short root feet. Preserve these simple EXACT facial features and bulb volume, NO mouth, no arms, no changing creature or extra leaves. This plant cannot walk with little human legs. Create a real CRAWL by reaching, planting and pulling with its long flexible tendril: frame1 bulb upright on root feet with large loop ready; frame2 long tendril UNCOILS forward to LEFT and down, body crouches on rear roots; frame3 tendril reaches far LEFT at ground level, tip curls like a hook/anchor, bulb still behind; frame4 hook stays planted and tendril bends to pull the bulb forward, front roots lift; frame5 pulling stroke is strongest, bulb tilts forward 10 degrees with rear roots trailing, head stays round and leaf stems flex; frame6 bulb arrives and root feet plant below it while tendril begins releasing anchor; frame7 tip lifts and tendril RECOILS into large loop over head, leaves follow through; frame8 settles back to original coiled silhouette ready for repeat. The long tendril remains one continuous green tube connected at leaf crown in every pose; never disappears or detaches. Show clear full-body reach-pull-recover stages readable at 64px. Keep the bulb's average root point and scale fixed in each slot, only small deliberate body shifts, but allow the vine's large silhouette arc. Ample left-side room for the extended tendril. Distinct complete drawings, not a rotating whole plant.

Create a production eight-frame animation of the approved little fantasy plant in Image2, using the approved-seed canvas Image1. The plant has a round olive bulb, two tiny glossy black eyes, four broad green leaves and two green curling vines. Preserve its identity, palette, size and painterly HD game-art style, fixed 3/4 left-facing view. This is a benign cute garden creature. One complete animation drawn in a single image: eight equally spaced whole-plant poses, one horizontal strip, transparent background, no text, no scenery, no shadow, clear padding between poses. Show locomotion by its long flexible vine reaching forward-left, resting against the ground, then gently pulling its bulb along while short roots lift and plant. Eight sequential stages: coiled resting vine; vine extending forward; vine tip lowered far to left; vine curves as the bulb leans forward and roots lift; bulb pulled forward; roots plant and stabilize; long vine lifts and recoils; original coiled silhouette returns smoothly. Keep the bulb round and the face exactly unchanged. The vine remains a single continuous tube connected at the leaf crown, never detached. The bulb should have only a small deliberate motion arc, with a stable common root location and scale in each frame. Large clearly changing vine silhouettes and root contacts must read at 64px. Full source drawings for real animation, not an idle-image wobble. No extra limbs, no mouth, no cut-off vine tips, no tiny variations repeated as eight frames.

Edit this approved cute garden character into one six-frame walking-cycle sprite sheet. Keep the same round green body, two black eyes, leafy crown and curved green stem. The little leaf feet reach forward, plant, pull the body ahead, recover, then repeat. Same camera, same character size, transparent background, no scenery or text. Draw every frame together in a roomy 3 by 2 grid.
